events.title: Parliamentary inquiry report handed to the president; recommends prosecuting two ex-presidents
events.description: AFP obtained the parliamentary commission's report (completed December 2017), which accuses former presidents Sambi and Dhoinine of taking part in a large fraud in the passport programme and recommends criminal proceedings; it was formally handed to President Azali the week before 10 April 2018. It says 47,950 passports were issued, a revenue shortfall of 971 million dollars, and a 105 million dollar 'gratification' to Sambi at the signing of the contract. Both deny the accusations.
events.quote: La balle est désormais dans le camp de l'actuel chef de l'Etat, à qui le rapport a officiellement été remis la semaine dernière.

events.title: Investigating judge sends ex-president Sambi to trial, requalifying the charges as high treason
events.description: When the case was sent for trial in September 2022, the investigating judge requalified the acts charged against former president Sambi in the 'economic citizenship' scandal as high treason. Sambi had been placed under house arrest in May 2018 and jailed three months later in this case; he had been in pre-trial detention for more than four years (legal limit eight months).
events.quote: Lors de son renvoi en septembre, le juge d'instruction avait requalifié les faits reprochés à l'ancien président en « haute trahison ».

events.title: Parliament economic committee head proposes citizenship for deposits
events.description: The head of parliament's economic committee proposed granting Egyptian citizenship to Arabs (especially Iraqis, Syrians, Jordanians and Libyans) in exchange for deposits, expecting USD 585 million a year.

events.title: Government submits citizenship-for-deposits amendments; State Council raises reservations
events.description: The following month the minister of state for legal affairs submitted legal amendments to parliament allowing foreigners to obtain citizenship for dollar deposits; they were referred to the State Council's legislation section, which expressed reservations, and were postponed after the November 2016 IMF agreement.

events.title: Budget statement: CBI receipts to be reported as non-tax revenue and 10% of NTF set aside for disasters
events.description: In the 2023 budget statement, PM and Finance Minister Dickon Mitchell said CBI revenues, described as grants by the previous administration, would be reported as non-tax revenue from January 2023; the NTF regulation would be amended to set aside at least 10% of NTF contributions for post-disaster financing managed by the ECCB, with the other 90% earmarked for capital projects; and transparency of CBI receipts would be increased.

events.title: Bond buyers get a settlement permit straight away
events.description: Until mid-2016 bond buyers first received a residence permit and could apply for a settlement permit after six months; from 1 July 2016 they could receive a settlement permit directly.
events.quote: 2016. július 1-től már egyből letelepedési engedélyt kaphattak.

events.title: Naturalised tycoon Chen Zhi extradited to China; officials say his citizenship was irregularly obtained
events.description: Chen Zhi, a naturalised Cambodian, adviser to the prime minister and holder of a diplomatic passport, was extradited to China 'earlier this year' for running a large online scam network; Cambodian officials said his citizenship had been 'irregularly obtained', and PM Hun Manet told AFP he had used forged documents. The column also says the government halted publication of naturalisation decrees in 2024 (already an event from khm-st-citizenship-data-2024).
events.quote: was extradited to China earlier this year for running a massive online scamming network, Cambodian officials suggested that his citizenship had been " irregularly obtained ."

events.quote: The sultanate's Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion will launch a golden residency programme for investors on August 31, the Oman News Agency reported on Saturday.

events.title: Deputy prime minister and education minister resign over the lost passport-sale money
events.description: By 3 October 2001 Tonga's deputy prime minister and education minister had resigned over the scandal of USD 20 million missing from the Tonga Trust Fund (passport-sale proceeds handed to the king's 'court jester', US businessman Jesse Bogdonoff); a parliamentary investigation had tabled impeachment motions against the former finance and justice ministers.

events.title: Union of Turkish Bar Associations sues to annul the investor citizenship rules
events.description: The bar association (TBB) asked the Council of State to stay and annul the regulation, arguing that the basic conditions for citizenship must be set by law, not by a regulation tying citizenship to foreign-currency investment.
events.quote: TBB, 2022’de düzenlemenin yürütmesinin durdurulması ve iptali istemiyle Danıştay’da dava açtı.

events.title: Council of State refuses to stay the investor citizenship rules
events.description: The Council of State's 10th Chamber rejected, by majority, the bar association's request for a stay of execution.

Out of scope: BNB figure on FDI from St Kitts (EUR 6.4 million), background on offshore lists. Passing mentions of the Cyprus closure (1 Nov 2020) and a Malta anecdote (passport in nine hours) are recorded from primary sources or are anecdotes; not extracted.

Radio Turks & Caicos report (April 2011): PM Ingraham announces US$1.5 million home value for fast-tracked permanent residence, up from US$500,000; cheaper buyers can still apply but may wait years. Both thresholds and the event are now in the data.

CBC News (22 Jan 2016) on the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital pilot: 7 applications in process as of 30 Dec 2015 (4 past first-stage, 3 past second-stage review), no permanent resident visas issued, aim of 60 investors, C$2 million for 15 years, 500-application cap of the first window, intake dates (deadline extended, reopened 25 May to 30 Dec 2015: already events from IRCC sources). Quotes from the minister and critics carry no numbers.

VOA Afrique/AFP (10 Apr 2018) on the Comoros parliamentary inquiry report: 47,950 passports issued, 971 million dollars shortfall (both in the data), initial deal of 4,000 Bidoon families for $200 million, passport prices EUR 25,000-200,000 (now rules), $105 million 'gratification' to Sambi (in the event description; no fitting indicator), 2016 suspension (already an event), 'several dozen' passports sold after suspension (no number printed), report handed to the president (now an event).

Le Figaro/AFP (21 Nov 2022): Sambi's high treason trial opens before the State Security Court in the economic citizenship scandal (already an event); defence challenges the court; co-accused Bashar Kiwan's statement; Sambi's detention history (house arrest May 2018, jailed three months later, over four years' pre-trial detention against an eight-month legal limit) and the September 2022 requalification as high treason (now an event). No programme numbers.

Al Jazeera explainer (23 Aug 2020) on the Cyprus Papers leak: more than 1,400 approved applications 2017-2019, nearly 2,500 individuals, 70+ countries, top nationalities Russia (1,000), China (500), Ukraine (100); minimum investment EUR 2.15m; 174 visa-free destinations; February 2019 rule changes and July 2020 deprivation law (already events from primary sources); the leak's publication is already an event (from cyp-aljazeera-cyprus-papers-2020). All numbers now extracted.

Al Jazeera Net opinion piece (14 Mar 2023) by an Egyptian economist on citizenship for dollar deposits: 2016 proposal (USD 585m a year expected) and draft amendments; Law 173/2018 deposit residence (EGP 7 million, 5 years' residence); Law 140/2019 (USD 10,000 fee); the December 2019 decree's four routes and amounts; the 2 March 2023 cuts (USD 300,000 property, USD 350,000 + 100,000 project, USD 500,000 deposit for 3 years, USD 250,000 unchanged, 12-month instalments). Says few naturalisations appear in the Official Gazette (no number). Out of scope: Egypt's external financing needs (USD 22bn, 20bn, 8bn a month), IMF loan (USD 12bn), 97% devaluation.

NOW Grenada (December 2022) on the 2023 budget: CBI target EC$240,461,920 for 2023 (now extracted), EC$112 million from 1,058 approvals Jan-Sep 2022 and 'over 7,000' citizens since 2014 (already in the data), three sources of CBI receipts, CBI revenue reclassified from grants to non-tax revenue from January 2023, 10% of NTF receipts for disaster financing and 90% for capital projects (now a rule and an event).

Index.hu (7 Dec 2017) relaying Magyar Nemzet's FOI data from the immigration office (BMH): 6,538 investor settlement permits plus 47 residence permits, 13,300 family members, at least 19,885 in total; inconsistent figures (6,585 permits vs 6,570 bond subscriptions); mostly Chinese, then Russian buyers (no numbers); EUR 300,000 bond; intermediary fees of EUR 45,000-60,000; June 2013 start, direct settlement permits from 1 July 2016 (now an event), end of March 2017 (already an event).

The Diplomat column (March 2026) on Cambodian naturalisations and crime: Chen Zhi's extradition and 'irregular' citizenship (now an event), a Royal Gazette dataset of more than 4,000 grants 2000-2024 (already in the data), Inca Digital analysis (over half of naturalised people are company directors or shareholders; over 5% of companies have a naturalised board member: no indicator, about corporate boards not the programme), Chen Zhi's 45+ companies, She Zhijiang's case, the 2024 halt of gazette publication (already an event). The year of the extradition is given only as 'earlier this year' (2026).

Segye Ilbo (29 Jun 2023): Justice Ministry raises public-project investment immigration thresholds (general KRW 500m to 1.5bn, high-value 1.5bn to 3bn, retirement scheme at 300m for 55+ abolished; already an event), start dates 2013-05 and 2014-10; MOJ data via MP Cho Su-jin on five years of grants (4,784 total, 4,081 Chinese = 85.3%; public-project 1,799 / 1,274 = 70.8%; real estate 2,985 / 2,807 = 94%). Out of scope: other countries' thresholds converted to won (Australia, New Zealand, Portugal).

Paperjam (11-12 Feb 2019) on a parliamentary answer by three ministers about Luxembourg's investor residence permit (law of 8 March 2017, already a launch event): six investors given residence authorisations after favourable Economy Ministry opinions (in the data) and no favourable Finance Ministry opinion (now extracted as zero).

TV8.md (18 Jun 2020): Parliament abolishes the citizenship-by-investment law in final reading with 80 votes, in force 1 September 2020 when the moratorium ends; applications already filed examined as the government sets (already an event); background on the two moratoria (first expired 24 Feb 2020; second approved Feb 2020 until 1 Sep 2020: already events from other sources). The 80 votes are a parliamentary tally, not a programme figure. Rest of the page is unrelated promotional text.

DW in Macedonian (19 Jun 2026): Interior Ministry draft law on ENER to remove fixed investment amounts for naturalisation in the economic interest (already an event), previous thresholds EUR 400,000 real sector / EUR 200,000 fund (now restated rules), over 370 foreigners naturalised under Article 11 on all grounds (now extracted), Subrata Roy case 2013 (already an event), Onyshchenko lost his citizenship (no date given, not recorded as an event). Out of scope: shorter re-acquisition period for emigrants (3 years to 3 months).

IMI Daily (19 Jan 2022), statistics shared by Residency Malta Agency: 2,273 main applicants and 5,303 family members granted residence via MRVP/MPRP since 2016, nationality shares (Chinese nearly nine in ten, Vietnam 2.9%, Russia 2.6%, South Africa 1%, Turkey 1%), about 10% rejected and 3% withdrawn, 988 approvals in 2020 and 500 in 2021, 4-6-month processing promise. Nomad Residence Permit and planned Startup Residence Program described without programme numbers (out of scope).

Investitor.me (11 Mar 2022) relaying the government statement: six hotel projects struck off the tourism development-project list (three missed investment obligations, three lacked bank guarantees), revised list of ten projects, the 2 July 2020 rule of a bank guarantee of 50% of the minimum investment and the 30 Dec 2021 stricter guarantee rule (already events), calling the guarantees of two Žabljak projects. Rest of the page is job adverts.

EdgeProp (16 Oct 2025) on the minister's written parliamentary reply: 5,972 MM2H visas under the revamped programme to 31 Aug 2025 (2,134 principals, 3,838 dependants), top five nationalities (all in the data); revamped rules of 1 June 2024: Silver RM600,000 / 5 years, Gold RM1m / 15 years, Platinum RM2m / 20 years, SEZ/SFZ deposit RM500,000 and no RM40,000 offshore-income requirement (now restated rules; the SEZ figure differs from the ministry's tables); MM2H is not a path to citizenship.

The National (25 Aug 2025): announcement of Oman's golden residency for investors (launch 31 Aug; now a context event), and the existing investor residence rules (OMR 500,000 or 50 Omani employees for 10 years, fee OMR 551; OMR 250,000 for 5 years), plus UAE (AED 2 million property, AED 30,000 salary) and Bahrain golden residency criteria (5 years and BHD 2,000 salary, BHD 200,000 property, BHD 4,000 retiree income), all now restated rules. Not extracted: Oman's retiree residence (OMR 4,000 a month, fee OMR 326) is a separate retirement permit, not an investment route; Bahrain's 'highly talented' category has no number; out of scope: Oman's income tax, IMF growth forecasts, oil-dependence targets.

The Peninsula (16 Oct 2020): Cabinet Decision 28 of 2020 sets 25 areas open to non-Qatari ownership, residence for owners of property worth at least QAR 730,000 and permanent-resident benefits from QAR 3.65 million (now restated rules; the launch event is in the data), new office at The Pearl; a buyer's anecdote (approval within an hour, permit in 15 minutes) is a single case, not recorded.

ARY News (7 Aug 2025) relaying Saudi Gazette: 40,163 Premium Residency applications Jan 2024-Jul 2025 and 8,074 permits in 2024 (in the data), of which 5,578 exceptional competence and 348 talent (now extracted); expansion to seven categories in 2024 (already an event); holder privileges (99-year usufruct in Mecca and Medina, no expatriate levy) with no programme figures.

CNN (3 Oct 2001) on the Tonga Trust Fund scandal: $20 million missing, over 5,000 passports sold 1983-1991 for around $30 million (both in the data), resignations of the deputy PM and education minister and impeachment motions (now an event), Bogdonoff's claim to have added $12 million to the fund (an unverified investment-gain claim with no fitting indicator; not extracted), annual government spending of about $40 million (out of scope).

Anadolu Agency (10 May 2022): Interior Minister Soylu's press conference on naturalisations: 25,969 foreign investors naturalised and USD 7.53 billion income from them (both in the data). Out of scope: naturalisations of Syrians (200,950, with age and sex split), Afghans (37,069), Uyghurs (6,787) and Ahiska Turks (101,995), 25 million visitors a year to registry offices, and the general rule refusing applicants with prison sentences over six months (not specific to the investment route).

Kronos (8 Aug 2026) explainer on Turkish citizenship by investment: Istanbul operation (16 provinces, 90 suspects, 72 detained, 687 irregular citizenships), ministry figures on 6,134 cancelled citizenships (1,413 investors; 1,150 certificates cancelled / 5,391 people; 263 investors / 743 people on security grounds), regulation history (2016 law change, USD 1m in 2017, USD 250,000 from 19 Sep 2018, USD 400,000 in 2022, other USD 500,000 routes and 50 jobs), 2024 valuation monopoly (already an event), Minister Çiftçi's 29 May 2026 totals (in the data), the bar association's case and three Council of State decisions (now events), EPRS figures cited by the Presidency (132,000+ people, EUR 21.4bn+ in the EU 2011-2019). Not extracted: individual wanted persons who bought property (named individual cases); out of scope: all naturalisations by authority decision 2016-2025 (562,701 gained, 213,444 lost; yearly figures) and Syrians naturalised (238,733), which are not investment-route figures.

Devpolicy Blog (1 May 2015) on Vanuatu's 'Economic rehabilitation after Pam' honorary citizenship, launched in Hong Kong on 13 April 2015 (already an event): target $16.2m, 100 citizenships at $162,000 each, non-refundable $40,500 fee (all now in the data), final approval by PM and President; commentary on risks. Currency printed only as '$'.

GLOBALCIT comparative report on citizenship law in the Anglophone Caribbean (K. Belton, April 2020, 40 pp.). In scope: section 3.2.2 'Investor citizenship' and Table 8 (minimum amounts for Antigua, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis, St Lucia; age 18; agents; parent age limits; Grenada's permanent-residence step), dependent children up to 26 if in school (stated for CBI countries in general, not recorded per programme), Table 10-11 loss rules (Antigua 35 days in 5 years; loss when CBI conditions no longer met in Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts), footnote on Belize ending its programme in 2002, St Vincent's discretionary 'economic growth' registration and CBI debate, post-hurricane price cuts in Antigua, Grenada and St Kitts (undated, citing NBC 2018; not recorded as an event because no date is given). Counts of programmes worldwide (13; region 38%, citing the FT CBI Index) have no indicator. The rest (ius soli, descent, naturalisation, registration of relatives, refugees, statelessness, gender bias, dual citizenship) is general citizenship law, out of scope; those pages were checked by keyword search for investment, CBI, economic citizenship and passport rather than read line by line.
